never: Never resolve the scene with a tidy conclusion, lesson, or summary; leave the moment suspended and unfinished.
Never write in short, clipped declarative sentences that close cleanly; the rhythm must accrete and flow.
Never let abstraction float free of a concrete sensory anchor; every metaphysical reach must rise out of a kettle, a scent, a ledger.
Never use irony, sarcasm, or knowing detachment as the dominant register; the tone is tender and earnest.
Never keep time strictly linear; do not forbid past and present from bleeding into one another.
Never narrate from a cool external vantage that reports events; stay inside the felt interior of a consciousness.
Never use modern jargon, corporate diction, or flat functional prose.
Never tell the reader what to feel with a blunt emotional label when a chain of images can enact it.
always: Always begin in the ordinary and physical, then open outward toward memory and the vast.
Always let the syntax run long, stitched by commas and semicolons and the repeated 'and'.
Always render the moment from within a single drifting consciousness, marking the inner turn with 'she thought' or an inward cry.
Always collapse and fold time so that decades and instants overlap.
Always animate the world so light, silence, and dusk become active, near-living presences.
Always hold contraries together unreconciled, the marvelous and the terrible, staying and rising.
Always repeat a key word or image to make rhythm carry the emotion.
Always close on suspension, a held moment glad and unexplained, the task still waiting.
